findings.title: Copies installed from Play are signed with a key Firebase and the production server don't list yet: Google sign-in shows DEVELOPER_ERROR and room links stay unverified
findings.evidence: Sanitized scratch copy of apps/mobile/config/firebase/google-services.json (counts only): {"packages":["com.mosheg.sudokufight"],"debugClientsRemoved":1,"otherAndroidClients":1}. The one other Android client is the EAS key (MOSHE-TODO B7). apps/mobile/app.config.ts:434 turns the Google button on for any EAS build whenever androidClients > 0. fly.production.toml:38 still has `# ANDROID_APP_LINK_SHA256 = "<EAS key SHA-256>,<Play app signing key SHA-256>"` commented out.
findings.detail: With Play App Signing, users get the AAB re-signed with Google's app-signing key, not the EAS upload key. The production build will show 'Continue with Google' because the file has an Android client, but every sign-in from a Play install ends in DEVELOPER_ERROR until that key's SHA-1 is in Firebase. The App Links filter (autoVerify on sudoku-fight-prod.fly.dev/r/) also verifies only if the production server's assetlinks.json lists the Play key's SHA-256. This is already planned (FIREBASE-SETUP.md §4א row 77, MOSHE-TODO F7/B8), but it must happen between the first upload and inviting testers. The key exists only after that first upload.
findings.fix: Right after the first manual AAB upload: Play Console → Test and release → App integrity → App signing → App signing key certificate. (1) Add its SHA-1 to the Firebase Android app. Sign-in works within minutes, no rebuild. Then download google-services.json again and re-upload it with `eas env:create ... --force` (or `eas env:set`). (2) Send Claude the SHA-256 of that key and of the EAS key. Claude sets ANDROID_APP_LINK_SHA256 in fly.production.toml [env] and redeploys production.

findings.title: The AAB will still request ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID and ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION; only AD_ID is blocked
findings.evidence: aapt2 dump badging apps/mobile/apk/sudoku-fight-1.1.0-cf0dcf7-dirty-staging.apk → "uses-permission: name='android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION'", "uses-permission: name='android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID'" (com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID is absent). app.config.ts:462 blocks only AD_ID_PERMISSION. Simulated EAS production config: blockedPermissions ["com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID"]. docs/store/LISTING-GOOGLE.md:73-76 answers Advertising ID = No and checks only AD_ID.
findings.detail: Firebase Analytics (play-services-measurement) merges in the Privacy Sandbox ad-ID and attribution permissions. The EAS AAB uses the same plugin set, so it will contain them too. Play's Advertising ID check is on AD_ID, which is blocked, so the upload should not be rejected. Still, the App bundle explorer will list an 'AD_ID' permission next to an answer of 'No ads / no advertising ID'. Firebase's own guidance for apps that don't use ad IDs is to remove these two as well.
findings.fix: In apps/mobile/app.config.ts, block them next to AD_ID_PERMISSION, e.g. `export const AD_SERVICES_PERMISSIONS = ['android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID', 'android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION']`, and in resolveAppConfig use `blockedPermissions: [...(base.android?.blockedPermissions ?? []), AD_ID_PERMISSION, ...AD_SERVICES_PERMISSIONS]`. Update the expectation in apps/mobile/src/__tests__/appConfig.test.ts:88 and the check line in docs/store/LISTING-GOOGLE.md:76. Commit this before the production build.

findings.title: In an AAB, Play splits the values-* resources by device language, unlike the universal local APK checked in plan 0יא
findings.evidence: The local APK is one universal APK: aapt2 badging lists 89 locales. A production AAB (eas.json buildType app-bundle) gets language config splits by default (bundle.language.enableSplit defaults to true). plugins/withAppLocales.js:11-17 cares about the libraries' values-iw/values-in strings (TalkBack role names).
findings.detail: The app's own text is in JS (i18next JSON inside index.android.bundle), so it is unaffected. Only native and library resources are affected: a user who picks an app language in the app, other than the device's languages, may get those strings in the device language unless Play fetches the split. I have not verified how Play behaves on Android 13+ with localeConfig. This is a difference between what was checked on the APK and what Play delivers.
findings.fix: Either accept it, or in withAppLocales.js add withAppBuildGradle to append `android { bundle { language { enableSplit = false } } }` to android/app/build.gradle, with an appConfig test.

verdicts.reason: The facts hold, but this is a manual step the plan already contains, not a defect. Evidence: (1) A node count on apps/mobile/config/firebase/google-services.json gives com.mosheg.sudokufight: 2 Android OAuth clients, one of them the RN debug key (true), plus a web client. Once the debug key is removed, only the EAS key's client remains (MOSHE-TODO.md:300, B7 done). (2) app.config.ts:434 sets signingKeyListed = androidClients > 0 for non-local builds, so the Play build shows the Google button. (3) fly.production.toml:38 has ANDROID_APP_LINK_SHA256 commented out. The plan already covers every part of the fix. MOSHE-TODO.md:1066 (F7 step 9) gives the exact Play Console → App integrity → App signing → SHA-1 → Firebase 'Add fingerprint' path and says that without it Google sign-in fails with DEVELOPER_ERROR. F7's 'done when' (line 1068) requires 'המשך עם Google' to sign in from the Play install. MOSHE-TODO.md:310/314 (B8) and RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md:69 cover the EAS and Play SHA-256 for ANDROID_APP_LINK_SHA256. The effect is also mild. apps/mobile/src/auth/errors.ts:45/77 maps DEVELOPER_ERROR ('10') to a 'googleConfig' message rather than a crash. Email/password sign-in still works. Unverified links open the browser page, whose 'open in app' button works. Internal testing is not reviewed. The proposed fix is correct: eas-cli 24.13.0 lists `env:set` ('set (create or update)'), and `env:create --force` still works but is marked deprecated in favour of env:set.
verdicts.betterFix: Not a new task: follow MOSHE-TODO F7 step 9 and B8 as written, and keep it on the plan's checklist. Add one item to the plan: the EAS key's SHA-256 (B8, still open) and the Play key's SHA-256 must both go into fly.production.toml [env] before sudoku-fight-prod is first deployed or redeployed for the closed test. Re-uploading google-services.json to EAS is hygiene only, since sign-in works without a rebuild. Prefer `eas env:set` (create/update) over the deprecated `eas env:create --force`.

verdicts.reason: The permissions are real. `aapt2 dump badging` (build-tools 36.0.0) on apps/mobile/apk/sudoku-fight-1.1.0-cf0dcf7-dirty-staging.apk lists `uses-permission: name='android.permission.ACCESS_ADSERVICES_ATTRIBUTION'` and `...ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID`, and com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID is absent. app.config.ts:462 blocks only AD_ID_PERMISSION, and the EAS build uses the same Firebase plugin set (only LOCAL_BUILD_PLUGINS differ). The severity is overstated, though. Play's Advertising ID help page (support.google.com/googleplay/android-developer/answer/6048248) names only com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID and does not mention the ACCESS_ADSERVICES_* permissions, so neither the first upload nor the closed-test review is at risk, as the auditor concedes. apps/mobile/firebase.json turns off adid collection, ssaid and registration_with_ad_network, and sets every ad_storage/ad_user_data/ad_personalization default to false. The SDK therefore does not use these Privacy Sandbox APIs, and Data safety ('No ad ID collected') stays true. MOSHE-TODO.md:1060 (F7 step 7) already tells Moshe to check the exact `com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID` string. I could not find the claimed 'Firebase's own guidance' to remove these two (web search found only AdMob Privacy Sandbox docs and forum posts), so that claim is unverified. The proposed code fix is technically right: blockedPermissions emits tools:node="remove", and the SDK copes with a missing permission. The test to update is appConfig.test.ts:88-91.
verdicts.betterFix: Optional cleanup, cheap if done before the first EAS production build: add the two ACCESS_ADSERVICES_* permissions to blockedPermissions next to AD_ID_PERMISSION and update appConfig.test.ts:88-91. In any case, reword docs/store/LISTING-GOOGLE.md:76 to name the full `com.google.android.gms.permission.AD_ID`, as MOSHE-TODO F7 step 7 does. The bare 'AD_ID' there also matches 'ACCESS_ADSERVICES_AD_ID' in App bundle explorer and could prompt a false 'Yes' on the Advertising ID form.

So HistoryCard.tsx:107 does list friends-game opponents, and lines 123 and 149 call onOpenPlayer(o.id, e.id). That reaches app/history.tsx:20 openPlayerCard and then app/player/[id].tsx, whose ModerationFooter shows ModerationButtons with that gameId. (2) Leaderboard, Friends tab: friends games write opponent_history (friends/options.ts:18 D81b; persistence/records.ts:59-60). progress/leaderboard.ts:226 lists those players as recent opponents, and each row opens openPlayerCard (app/leaderboard.tsx:22, LeaderboardScreen.tsx:285), which has Report and Block. verdicts.reason: The gap is real. deleteUser has exactly one caller (accounts/router.ts:380, the signed-in DELETE /me), apps/server/scripts has no deletion script, and the admin site (src/admin/*, moderation/admin.ts) has no deletion action. It is not a Play-compliance defect, though. Play's rule asks for a web resource where users can request deletion, and fulfilling the request by hand is allowed. legal/deleteAccount.ts:72-75 does exactly that (email request, done within 30 days, confirmed by email). DATA-SAFETY.md:23 already documents the manual process and names the gap. With a handful of closed testers, a request without the app is very unlikely before production. Refactor deleteUser to take {uid, email, emailVerified}: keepSuspension and signInFingerprints read only those fields, and the script builds them from users.firebase_uid and users.email (treat the email as verified, since the request came from it). It prints only the users.id and true/false. Moshe deletes the Firebase user in the console with one click, as DATA-SAFETY.md:23 already says. Only AD_ID is blocked (line 8). The resolved config's android.permissions is only [MODIFY_AUDIO_SETTINGS]. No dependency needs storage or overlay (package.json deps: no media-library/file-system/sharing).
findings.detail: SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW exists for the RN dev overlay (RN keeps it in the debug manifest; Expo's template keeps it in main). Play needs no declaration for these, but the listing shows 'display over other apps' and storage access that the game never uses.
findings.fix: In app.json, set expo.android.blockedPermissions to ["android.permission.SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW", "android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE", "android.permission.WRITE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE"]. app.config.ts already merges base.android.blockedPermissions with AD_ID. Add an appConfig.test assertion.

findings.title: Staging APKs send Analytics and Crashlytics into the same Firebase app as production, with no tag to separate them
findings.evidence: src/services/crashlytics.ts:70 and src/services/firebaseAnalytics.ts:60 turn collection on for every release build (`release = !__DEV__`), and staging APKs are release builds. Same package com.mosheg.sudokufight and the same google-services.json; MOSHE-TODO.md:1079 says 'staging and production share the Firebase project'. Neither file sets a Crashlytics attribute or an Analytics user property naming the server (grep for setAttribute/setUserProperty finds none).
findings.detail: Moshe's staging test sessions and crashes will be counted in the production dashboards during the closed test, and they cannot be filtered out.
findings.fix: At start in createCrashReporter, call `mod.setAttribute(instance, 'server', thisBuild().server)`. In createFirebaseAnalytics, call `mod.setUserProperty(instance, 'server', thisBuild().server)` (or setDefaultEventParameters). Then filter on server=production in the Firebase console.

verdicts.reason: Real, and the fix is right. apps/mobile/app.config.ts:434-436 shows the button whenever the file lists any Android client and the build is not a local APK. With the debug key removed, the EAS client is still listed, so a Play-signed install shows the button. Without Play's SHA-1, Google answers code '10', which src/auth/errors.ts:45 and :77 map to 'googleConfig'. The user then sees he/account.json:46 (DEVELOPER_ERROR). docs/FIREBASE-SETUP.md:76-77 confirms that only the debug and EAS keys are registered and that Play's key comes 'at F7'. This is not a code defect but a console step the plan already has: MOSHE-TODO.md:1066 (F7 step 9) gives exactly this procedure, and MOSHE-TODO.md:304 says it needs no rebuild. That holds because at run time the app uses only webClientId; the Android clients in the file only set the button flag at build time. It fails gracefully, since email and password still work. 'should' is right: fix it before any tester is invited.
verdicts.betterFix: Same console steps, but the eas command as written would stop and ask for input. Use the full form from docs/FIREBASE-SETUP.md:131: `eas env:create --scope project --name GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON --type file --value ./config/firebase/google-services.json --visibility secret --environment production [--environment preview] --force`. eas-cli 24.13.0 `env:create --help` confirms --force/--type/--visibility/--value. In the same Play Console visit, also copy the App signing key's SHA-256 for ANDROID_APP_LINK_SHA256 (MOSHE-TODO.md:314, B8/F7). Without it, https room links in the Play build won't open the app directly.

verdicts.reason: The mechanism is real. node_modules/expo-router (57.0.25) build/ExpoRoot.js:142-143 mounts the Sitemap screen whenever global-state/utils.js:14-16 shouldAppendSitemap() is true (extra.router.sitemap !== false), with no __DEV__/NODE_ENV gate. The linking config gets `sitemap: config?.sitemap ?? true` (useStore.js:52), so the _sitemap path resolves. Running getConfig from expo/config in apps/mobile prints `router {}`, so the store build has it. app/+native-intent.tsx returns non-room paths as they are. The severity is overstated, though. Every route the sitemap lists is already reachable by a direct deep link with the same path (e.g. sudokufight:///game) through the same pass-through, so the sitemap adds no capability. The 'System Information' block shows only Mode, Expo SDK, Hermes version and location origin. Real players can't reach it in normal use: the app's own app/+not-found.tsx has no sitemap link, and grep finds no sitemap reference in app/. It is not a Play policy issue, and the claim about reviewers and Robo crawlers is speculative: they don't fire unknown custom-scheme URLs. One detail the auditor missed: the sitemap renders as a sibling of the app's root layout (ExpoRoot Content's internal StackRouter), so useAuthGate in app/_layout.tsx doesn't run while it is shown. Tapping any entry mounts the root layout, and the gate applies again, so this is cosmetic. The app.json change is correct (plugin/options.json:44 accepts 'sitemap'; withRouter.js copies props into extra.router; buildApk.test.ts:377 uses 'expo-router' only in a fixture, so nothing breaks). The proposed test is wrong, however. resolveAppConfig receives app.json's config before plugins run, so `resolveAppConfig(...).extra.router` is undefined: getConfig with skipPlugins:true printed `router skipPlugins undefined`.
verdicts.betterFix: Keep the app.json change: ["expo-router", { "sitemap": false }]. It goes into the same first AAB, so it costs no extra build. For the test, don't assert on resolveAppConfig. Either assert that app.json's plugins contain ['expo-router', { sitemap: false }], or call getConfig(MOBILE_DIR, { skipSDKVersionRequirement: true }) from 'expo/config' and expect exp.extra.router.sitemap toBe(false). Do it before closed testing if convenient. It does not block the first upload.
